identity.name: Legacy Machine 101
identity.one_liner: MB&F's most accessible Legacy Machine, built around a single oversized balance wheel raised above the dial on its own bridge rather than the twin-balance layout of the earlier LM1 and LM2.

provenance_events.description: MB&F's Legacy Machine 101 (LM101) debuts as the brand's most "classical" piece: a suspended balance wheel above a sub-dial, with a 45mm case and an in-house movement. MB&F positions it as a "watchmaker's watch" — the simplest, most personal piece in the Horological Machine catalogue.

narrative.story: MB&F built its reputation on the more overtly mechanical, twin-balance-wheel Legacy Machine 1 and 2 before releasing LM101 in 2014 as a single-complication, single-balance simplification of the same visual language: a large balance wheel suspended on an arched bridge above a dial dominated by hours, minutes, and a power-reserve indicator. Max Büsser founded MB&F in 2005 after leaving executive roles at Jaeger-LeCoultre and Harry Winston, describing the company as a horological research lab rather than a conventional manufacture; LM101 was the model that made that lab's output ownable at a lower entry point than the rest of the Legacy Machine line.
narrative.collector_notes: The movement was co-developed with independent watchmaker Kari Voutilainen, and finishing quality on early production runs is a frequent point of comparison collectors make against Voutilainen's own eponymous watches.
